title: Fix/flicker reduction rework
author: spencer426
body:
## Summary

 Fixes UI flicker and instability by dynamically constraining the main content area's height, ensuring it never overflows the terminal.

## Details
  The Gemini CLI UI previously experienced flicker, particularly when the conversation history or the multi-line input composer grew beyond the terminal's visible area. This PR resolves the
  issue by introducing a dynamic height management system.

  Specifically:
   - A ResizeObserver is now used in DefaultAppLayout.tsx to continuously measure the exact height of the input composer area (uiState.mainControlsRef).
   - This composerHeight is then passed as a prop to MainContent.tsx.
   - Inside MainContent.tsx, the MainContent component (which renders the App Header and Conversation History) is wrapped in an existing <MaxSizedBox> component.
   - The maxHeight prop of MaxSizedBox is dynamically set to availableTerminalHeight - composerHeight.

  This ensures that the combined height of the history and header never exceeds the available vertical space, preventing UI overflow and eliminating the root cause of the flicker during
  re-renders and content updates. Necessary mocks for ResizeObserver were added to App.test.tsx and test-setup.ts to ensure test stability.

## Related Issues
  Fixes #4245

title: docs: fix incorrect tool parameter names across reference pages
author: subratomandal
body:
I was going through the docs and comparing them against the source
code, and noticed quite a few tool parameter names that are out of
sync. I have corrected them.

Most of the issues were in docs/tools/file-system.md:
 1. read_file had offset and limit as params but the source actually
  uses start_line and end_line (1-based, inclusive)
 2. grep_search had path instead of dir_path, include instead of
  include_pattern, and was missing a few params entirely
  (exclude_pattern, names_only, max_matches_per_file, total_max_matches)
 3. glob had path instead of dir_path and was missing respect_gemini_ignore

A couple smaller things in the other files:
 1. grep_search in docs/reference/tools.md also had include wrong
 2. exit_plan_mode had plan instead of plan_path
 3. --approval-mode in the CLI reference was missing plan as a valid option
 4. subagents page had generalist_agent but the source just calls it generalist

I double checked all of this against base-declarations.ts,
default-legacy.ts, config.ts, and generalist-agent.ts so it
should be accurate.

## TLDR

Added `micro` to the list of supported editors.
More information: https://micro-editor.github.io/

Issue #4744 

## Dive Deeper

### Why support `micro`:

Users like micro editor because it provides a modern, user-friendly alternative to other terminal-based text editors like `nano` and `vim` by offering familiar shortcuts, built-in features like mouse support and syntax highlighting, and an extensive plugin system for added functionality and customization, all within a single, easy-to-install binary. It's ideal for users who find `nano` too basic but `vim` too complex, wanting a powerful, intuitive experience directly in the terminal. 

### Summary of changes

This pull request adds support for the Micro terminal-based text editor throughout the codebase. The changes ensure that `micro` is recognized as a valid editor, can be launched for editing and diffing, and is properly handled in both normal and sandboxed environments. micro has been added to the test matrix.

* Implemented logic in `getDiffCommand` to open both files side by side in Micro, since it lacks a built-in diff mode.
* Updated terminal editor checks to include Micro, ensuring it is handled like other terminal-based editors for launching and closing.
* Allowed Micro to be used in sandboxed environments, similar to other terminal editors.
* Expanded and added tests to cover Micro in editor command resolution, diff launching, sandbox permissions, and availability checks.

The `MERGE` conflict resolution strategy is implemented to overwrite the file, which is misleading and can lead to unintentional data loss. The comment `// For now, overwrite (could be enhanced with LLM-based merging)` acknowledges this, but this behavior is dangerous for a strategy named "MERGE". This should either implement a safe merge or throw an error to prevent data loss until a proper merge strategy is implemented.

```typescript
      case ConflictResolution.MERGE:
        // True merge is not yet implemented. Throw an error to prevent data loss.
        throw new Error(`File conflict: ${filePath} requires a merge, but auto-merging is not yet implemented. Please resolve manually.`);
```

The `CodeGenerationAgent` is incorrectly assigned `AgentType.ANALYSIS_INSIGHT`. This creates a collision with `AnalysisInsightAgent`, which is also registered with the same type. When both agents are registered in `initializeDefaultAgents`, the second registration will overwrite the first in the `agents` map, meaning one of these agents will never be triggered.

A unique agent type should be created for `CodeGenerationAgent` in the `AgentType` enum (e.g., `CODE_GENERATION = 'code_generation'`) and then used here.

```typescript
  readonly type = AgentType.CODE_GENERATION; // Using a unique type for this agent
```

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The `VFSEditTool` constructor creates a new `VirtualFileSystem` instance. This is a critical design flaw because it defeats the purpose of having a centralized, consistent view of the file system. Each invocation of `vfs-edit` will have its own isolated cache, leading to race conditions, stale data, and an inability to resolve conflicts between different edits.

The `VirtualFileSystem` should be a singleton or a shared instance provided through dependency injection to ensure all tools operate on the same consistent state.
